prediction.likelyOutcome: LBJ Venture will almost certainly obtain judgment for its deficiency-based unpaid rent (roughly $78,000-$96,000) plus attorneys' fees (likely close to the $67,000 requested, subject to Rohrmoos proof), but is more likely than not to lose the acceleration theory given the lease's 'if Landlord does not relet' conditional language and the fact that LBJ Venture did relet. The $300,000 kitchen claim is very unlikely to be awarded given the total absence of value/damages evidence at trial. Net expected recovery is well below the $905,000 requested, landing more plausibly in the low-to-mid $200,000s.

issues.label: Base Unpaid Rent (Deficiency Method Under Section 10.02(b))
Rent Acceleration Theory (Incremental Amount Above Deficiency)
Attorneys' Fees Under Tex. Civ. Prac. & Rem. Code § 38.001 and Lease § 12.01

outcome.description: After the bench trial the trial court rendered judgment for the landlord of $96,072.49 (unpaid rent through trial net of replacement-tenant rent, late fees, and prejudgment interest) — the figure the tenant advocated, roughly one-tenth of the more than $900,000 the landlord sought — plus 18% post-judgment interest, and awarded $0 in attorneys' fees. The court of appeals affirmed the damages award and reversed only the denial of attorneys' fees, remanding for a determination of a reasonable fee under the lease.
outcome.finalNote: Damages affirmed; fee denial reversed and remanded.
